channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan Establishes New System for Public Security Training
item.description: Uzbekistan is launching a new continuous education system to train professionals in public security. The initiative aims to equip personnel with modern knowledge and practical skills. A presidential decree emphasizes improving the system for public security personnel, transforming the University of Public Security into a core institution.

item.title: Uzbekistan Hosts International Seminar on Green Economy and WTO Law
item.description: An international seminar on "Green Economy, Energy, and Investment Law within WTO Law" was held in Uzbekistan. The event, in cooperation with the Konrad Adenauer Foundation, discussed WTO principles, Uzbekistan's accession, green economy, renewable energy, carbon taxes, and foreign investment regulation. The goal is to prepare lawyers for new economic conditions.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces New Opportunities and Legal Guarantees for Entrepreneurs
item.description: A roundtable in Tashkent discussed new opportunities and legal guarantees for entrepreneurs, following a presidential decree. The event highlighted support mechanisms, rights protection for businesses, and state policy prospects. Significant measures include a three-year moratorium on inspections for small businesses and leniency for first-time minor offenses.

item.title: Russians unfit for military service may be tasked with countering drones
item.description: Individuals in Russia deemed unfit for military service may be eligible to sign contracts with the Ministry of Defense. These individuals would not be sent to the front lines but would focus on protecting strategic sites from drone threats within the country.

item.title: EAEU countries to implement unified rules for marketplace returns
item.description: Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) member states will adopt unified rules for returning goods purchased from online marketplaces. An agreement on e-commerce, signed in Cholpon-Ata, establishes common consumer protection standards for cross-border purchases within the union. Buyers will have a 14-day period to return quality goods.

item.title: Uzbekistan proposes fines for failure to report underage pregnancies and early marriages
item.description: Uzbekistan is considering imposing fines on individuals who fail to report cases of early marriage or pregnancies of minors under 16. The proposed legislation targets those obligated to inform internal affairs bodies or "Inson" centers but who neglect this duty.

item.title: Germany is Priority Destination for New Direct Flights from Kyrgyzstan, Says Cabinet Head
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering opening direct flights to Europe, with Germany as the priority destination, announced the head of the Cabinet of Ministers. Following removal from the EU's aviation safety blacklist, Kyrgyzstan aims to develop startup ecosystems and IT, proposing joint working groups with Germany.

item.title: Personnel Changes Occur in Uzbekistan's Chamber of Accounts and Presidential Administration
item.description: Uzbekistan's Chamber of Accounts and Presidential Administration's Compliance Service have seen personnel changes. Two deputy heads of the Chamber of Accounts were appointed to new positions, and two other officials took deputy roles within the department. The changes were signed by the head of the Presidential Administration.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Creates AI-Animated Film Based on "Manas" Epic
item.description: A seven-minute excerpt of an AI-animated film based on the "Manas" epic was presented in Kyrgyzstan. The project, a collaboration between the Ministry of Culture and other entities, aims to present the epic to younger generations using artificial intelligence and new visual solutions. The full version is planned for release on December 4.

item.title: Three Kyrgyz enterprises gain export rights to European market
item.description: Three Kyrgyz enterprises have received the right to export to the European market. This was discussed during a meeting of the Kyrgyz-German Business Council in Cholpon-Ata, where participants focused on developing small and medium-sized businesses, winter tourism, and the IT sector.

item.title: Kremlin: Putin's talks with Trump envoys were substantive and confidential
item.description: The Kremlin described President Vladimir Putin's meetings with US special envoy Stephen Whitocoff and Jared Kushner as substantive, frank, and confidential. The talks, lasting over three hours, covered the situation in the conflict zone, Russian military successes, and potential US-Russia economic projects.

item.title: Uzbekistan's top 10 foreign trade partners revealed for first seven months
item.description: Uzbekistan has conducted trade with over 200 countries in the first seven months of the year. The National Statistics Committee has announced the country's top 10 foreign trade partners during this period.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Celebrates Independence Amidst SCO Summit and World Nomad Games
item.description: Kyrgyzstan marked its 35th Independence Day with a focus on the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in Bishkek. The summit, chaired by President Sadyr Japarov, addressed regional security, economic ties, and transport corridors, resulting in the Bishkek Declaration. A new center to combat transnational organized crime will be established in Bishkek.

item.title: Putin Discusses Ukraine Settlement with Trump Envoys in Moscow
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin met with Donald Trump's special envoy Stephen Witkoff and advisor Jared Kushner in Moscow to discuss the Ukrainian settlement. Putin stated that Russian forces had not struck Kyiv since September 5, and noted that Ukrainian forces had also reduced attacks on Russia. He expressed high trust in Witkoff and Kushner as mediators.

item.title: Uzbekistan Adopts European Experience for Banking Sector Development
item.description: Uzbekistan is actively reforming its banking system, focusing on digitalization and expanding financial access, inspired by European practices. A recent seminar in the Czech Republic for Uzbek banking professionals aimed to enhance their skills in digital technologies, risk assessment, and customer needs, aligning with national human capital development goals.

item.title: Member of Parliament Meets with Youth in Yangier
item.description: Legislative Chamber member Gavhar Alimova met with youth in Yangier to discuss problems and initiatives. The dialogue focused on dual education, practical skills, employer needs, and youth employment. Graduates are finding legal work in Germany after completing German language courses at the technical school.

item.title: Modern facilities established at Nasaf customs post in Kashkadarya region
item.description: The Nasaf customs post in Qarshi has moved to a new administrative building meeting modern requirements. A customs warehouse was also renovated and its territory improved. This modern infrastructure aims to enhance customs service efficiency and facilitate foreign trade. Over eight months, the post processed 1,964 customs inspections, collecting over 377 billion soums in customs payments.

item.title: Uzbekistan Opens First Consulate in Seattle, USA, to Boost Bilateral Ties
item.description: Uzbekistan has officially opened its first consulate in the northwestern United States, located in Seattle. Presidential advisor Komil Allamjonov stated the consulate will further develop Uzbek-US relations, focusing on trade, investment, technology, education, and people-to-people exchanges.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Pakistan Boost Trade Towards Investment and Joint Production
item.description: A business forum in Karachi focused on expanding trade and economic cooperation between Uzbekistan and Pakistan, aiming to attract investment and launch joint production projects. Discussions covered opportunities in textiles, pharmaceuticals, agriculture, and logistics. Arif Habib Group and Al Karam textile company expressed interest in investing and establishing joint ventures in Uzbekistan.

item.title: Appointments Made at Accounts Chamber and Presidential Administration
item.description: New deputies have been appointed to the Accounts Chamber chairman's office, and a new head has been appointed to the compliance service department of the Presidential Administration, according to relevant orders from the administration head.

item.title: Youth Initiatives in Achieving Sustainable Development Goals to Be Supported in Uzbekistan
item.description: A special session at the Global Conference of Young Parliamentarians in Samarkand focused on parliamentary roles in achieving Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Uzbekistan highlighted progress in poverty reduction (from 17% to 5.8%), unemployment (from 10.5% to 5.1%), and higher education enrollment (to 47.7%). Parliaments are crucial for legislative frameworks and citizen engagement.

item.title: Unpleasant Odor Eliminated at Tashkent's 'Salar' Wastewater Treatment Facility
item.description: Tashkent city administration reports the installation of a 9.5 billion soum filtration system at the 'Salar' wastewater treatment facility has eliminated unpleasant odors. The system, imported from Russia, uses a three-stage filtration process involving catalytic sorbent and activated carbon, reducing hydrogen sulfide and ammonia levels to zero.

item.title: US Strikes Three Iranian Oil Tankers; Crew Safely Evacuated
item.description: The United States struck three Iranian oil tankers, leading to the safe evacuation of their crews. This action followed an attack by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps on American vessels with ballistic missiles.

item.title: Uzbekistan Organizes International Seminar on Green Economy and WTO Law
item.description: An international seminar-training on "Law of the Green Economy, Energy, and Investments within WTO Law" was held in Uzbekistan. The event focused on the interconnectedness of international trade, investment, energy, and environmental protection, particularly in light of Uzbekistan's accession to the WTO. Discussions covered WTO principles, trade and environmental balance, and energy law.

item.title: Uzbek President to Pay Official Visit to Serbia
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will visit Serbia on September 7-8 for an official visit at the invitation of Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić. High-level talks and a business forum are scheduled in Belgrade to discuss strengthening bilateral partnership, expanding trade and economic cooperation, and joint projects in priority sectors. Agreements on labor migration and cultural ties are also expected.

item.title: Youth Voices from Samarkand Conference to Translate into Action
item.description: The XII Global Conference of Young Parliamentarians in Samarkand discussed youth rights, political participation, education, and digital security. Laylo Aslanova, Chairperson of the Youth Parliament of the Senate of Uzbekistan, highlighted the increasing role of youth in political life and decision-making processes, attributing these opportunities to state policy and gender equality efforts.

item.title: Osh-Kara-Suu Road Repairs Nearing Completion, Set to Finish in November
item.description: Major repairs on the Osh-Kara-Suu road are in their final stages, with completion scheduled for November. Over 100 heavy machinery units are currently deployed on the 19-kilometer section. The road is being widened to four lanes, with sidewalks and a bicycle lane under construction. The project costs 2.5 billion soms.

item.title: Uzbekistan Discusses Digitalization Priorities with Young Specialists
item.description: Uzbekistan's Minister of Digital Technologies met with young specialists to discuss effective use of their knowledge and potential. Topics included improving government processes, simplifying procedures, and reducing bureaucracy. The minister emphasized using modern technologies, especially AI, to automate internal processes, boost productivity, and accelerate decision-making. R&D and innovation were also prioritized.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Highlights Mountain Agenda at Istanbul Climate Summit
item.description: Kyrgyzstan presented its mountain agenda priorities at an international climate financing summit in Istanbul. The delegation urged increased climate finance for developing nations, focusing on adaptation and resilience in vulnerable regions. They also proposed establishing a Global Center for Climate Resilience of Mountain Regions in Bishkek.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Gains Access to Export Raspberries, Tayberries, and Currants to China
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has obtained permission to export raspberries, tayberries, and currants to China, following agreements signed during Chinese President Xi Jinping's state visit. The Minister of Water Resources, Agriculture, and Processing Industry noted the Chinese market's strict requirements and the substantial work involved. Farmers interested in exporting are encouraged to contact the ministry.

item.title: Year-Round Ethno-Village Planned for Kyrgyzstan's Kyrchyn Gorge
item.description: Plans are underway to construct a year-round ethno-village in Kyrgyzstan's Kyrchyn Gorge, capable of hosting visitors throughout the year. The project aims to significantly expand the current facilities, providing necessary infrastructure for tourists and addressing existing shortcomings. The entrance to the future ethno-village will be paid.

item.title: Citizens can now track their appeals sent to Presidential Public Reception offices via SMS
item.description: Citizens can now track their appeals submitted to Presidential Public Reception offices. The Presidential Public Reception, in collaboration with the Ministry of Digital Technologies, has launched an SMS notification service for feedback. Details are available via the provided link.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Explores Digital Som Launch and Blockchain Development
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov chaired a council meeting on virtual assets and blockchain, discussing the potential pilot launch of the digital som and KGST stablecoin development. Key topics included market development, regulation, security, taxation, and international cooperation. The National Bank will pilot the digital som by 2026.

item.title: Tanzila Narbayeva: Parliaments Must Drive Sustainable Development
item.description: Speaking at the XII Global Conference of Young Parliamentarians, Tanzila Narbayeva stated that parliaments should be a driving force for sustainable development, not just observers. Young parliamentarians discussed involving youth in legislation, parliamentary oversight, and inter-parliamentary cooperation to accelerate the SDGs.

item.title: Global Wheat and Sugar Prices Rise in August, FAO Reports
item.description: Global wheat and sugar prices increased in August, according to the FAO. Wheat prices rose 2.6% monthly and 15% annually, while sugar prices jumped 11.9% in August. Factors include Black Sea export disruptions, European weather, and reduced production in Brazil. Kyrgyzstan relies on imports for sugar and wheat.

item.title: Uzbekistan focuses on social sector modernization and human capital development
item.description: Uzbekistan is modernizing its social sector and developing human capital through education reform, improved healthcare, and enhanced social assistance for low-income families. Strategic priorities include science, technology, digitalization, and artificial intelligence to build a competitive economy. The government emphasizes youth involvement in reforms and regional development through new infrastructure and improved living standards.

item.title: Tallest bridge on China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway under construction in Suzak
item.description: The tallest bridge on the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway route is being built across the Kech-Alat River in Kyrgyzstan's Suzak district. The structure will be over 956 meters long with piers reaching 96 meters, totaling 122 meters in height. Foundation work is complete, with pier and abutment construction ongoing.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan proposes consolidating crypto market regulation under one body
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering consolidating licensing, regulation, and oversight of virtual asset market participants into a single state body. Currently, the National Agency for Virtual Assets (NAVA) handles licensing and regulation, while the Financial Supervision Agency oversees participants. This consolidation aims to reduce administrative burdens and avoid duplicated functions.

item.title: Uzbekistan reduces poverty, focusing on quality of life and income growth
item.description: Uzbekistan has reduced its needy population from 2.2 million to 1.5 million this year, with unemployment and poverty eliminated in 49 districts and 3429 mahallas. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev emphasized that poverty reduction requires more than just funding, stressing targeted approaches, leadership accountability, and results-orientation. The focus is on improving quality of life, stable income growth, and citizen confidence.

item.title: Presidential advisor Gofurjon Mirzayev dismissed from post
item.description: Gofurjon Mirzayev has been dismissed from his position as a presidential advisor. According to a source, he is expected to be appointed as the chairman of the Mahalla Association, replacing Kahramon Kuronboyev.
